problem.title: Getting a repeat prescription takes four phone calls and two trips, every single month
problem.description: Somebody managing three long-term conditions orders their repeat from the surgery, waits two working days, then rings the pharmacy to find out whether it arrived, then goes in to be told one item is out of stock and the others are not ready. It takes about a week of low-level chasing every month, and the people doing the chasing are the people least able to do it: older, often unwell, often without transport.

shortcomings.text: Orders well, then goes silent about everything that happens next
Says nothing about whether the pharmacy actually has the item
Assumes a smartphone and the confidence to use it
Engaged at exactly the times somebody is free to ring
The answer is usually ring back tomorrow

existingSolutions.text: Repeat dispensing arranged by the surgery

shortcomings.text: Excellent when it is set up, and almost nobody is offered it
Falls over the moment a dose changes

existingSolutions.text: Just going to the pharmacy and hoping

shortcomings.text: Two trips more often than one
Hardest on exactly the people who find trips hardest

functional.text: Have the tablets in my hand before the current box runs out
Make one trip rather than three
Find out about an out-of-stock item before setting off, not at the counter

emotional.text: Stop worrying about running out of a medicine I cannot stop taking
Stop feeling like a nuisance for ringing again

social.text: Not have to ask my daughter to sort it out again

problem.contextWhen: Every month, starting about a week before the current supply runs out, and urgently once it has.
problem.customerDescription: People on three or more repeat medications, mostly over sixty-five, and the family members who do the chasing on their behalf.

solutions.title: Track it like a parcel
solutions.description: One text per stage: request received by the surgery, prescription signed, sent to the pharmacy, dispensed, ready to collect. Nothing is asked of the patient and no app is needed. It does not make the process faster, it makes it visible, which removes every one of the chasing phone calls.
solutions.inspirationDetail: Straight from parcel tracking. The wait is tolerable when you know where the thing is.
solutions.analogyInsight: Visibility is worth more than speed when the wait is unavoidable.

solutions.title: Tell people about out-of-stock items before they set off
solutions.description: A stock check against the pharmacy's own system at the moment the prescription arrives, so the patient is told the same day that one of four items will be a week late, rather than finding out at the counter.
solutions.inspirationDetail: Took the existing NHS App flow and asked what the single most useful missing message would be.

improveIdeas.communication: Say what is out of stock, on the day

solutions.title: A monthly delivery subscription
solutions.description: A pharmacy that posts everything monthly on a fixed date, with no ordering step at all.
solutions.inspirationDetail: Eliminate: remove the collection trip entirely.

rootCauses.description: Three organisations hold one piece of information between them and none of them owns it
The patient is the only thing connecting the surgery, the pharmacy and the wholesaler
Nothing tells anyone that a step has finished

affectedGroups.name: Patients on multiple repeats
affectedGroups.description: Do the chasing monthly, while unwell.

affectedGroups.name: Family carers
affectedGroups.description: Take on the chasing, usually remotely and during their own working hours.

affectedGroups.name: Pharmacy staff
affectedGroups.description: Spend a large part of every day answering the same phone call.

affectedGroups.name: GP reception
affectedGroups.description: Field the calls that should have gone to the pharmacy.

workspace.rootCauseNotes: Nobody in the chain is doing anything wrong. The patient is simply the only messaging system between three organisations that do not talk to each other.
workspace.analogyInsight: A fourteen pound parcel tells you it has been picked, packed, dispatched and is three stops away. A month of medication tells you nothing at all.
